## Constants

### blamed

The pull requests a commit says were bugs: the one a revert undoes, or the one a fix names.

```ts
const blamed: (commit: Pick<Commit, "subject" | "body">) => number[];
```

### breaches

Each band the scorecard breaks, as a sentence with its fix.

```ts
const breaches: (card: Scorecard, ratchet: Ratchet) => string[];
```

### CANDIDATES

Where `mine --write` puts the draft, beside the cases a person finishes.

```ts
const CANDIDATES = ".sdlc/replz/rule-candidates.md";
```

### candidatesMarkdown

The draft file: each candidate, its pull requests and one finding from each, for a person to accept or delete.

```ts
const candidatesMarkdown: (candidates: readonly Candidate[], meta: {
    readonly slug: string;
    readonly since: string;
    readonly findings: number;
}) => string;
```

### DEFAULT_CANDIDATES

Ten candidates: enough to pick from, few enough to read.

```ts
const DEFAULT_CANDIDATES = 10;
```

### DEFAULT_DAYS

Thirty days: long enough for a fix to land after the change it repairs, short enough to move.

```ts
const DEFAULT_DAYS = 30;
```

### digest

```ts
const digest: (textOf: string) => string;
```

### findingsOf

The findings in one comment. An inline comment is one finding. A summary comment holds as many
as it has lines that open with a severity tag; its counts line (`0 [Important], 1 [Nit]`) and
everything else in it are not findings.

```ts
const findingsOf: (comment: Comment) => Finding[];
```

### firstDifference

The first line the two texts disagree on, counted from 1, and each side's version of it.

```ts
const firstDifference: (base: string, head: string) => {
    readonly line: number;
    readonly base: string;
    readonly head: string;
};
```

### ghQueries

The `gh api` paths and jq filters whose lines `parseComments` reads, given the repo and a since date.

```ts
const ghQueries: (slug: string, since: string) => readonly (readonly string[])[];
```

### gradePrompt

The grader's whole prompt: the answer key, one finding, and the question.

```ts

```

### isCode

Code whose lines can carry a bug; tests, fixtures, docs, snapshots and generated files cannot.

```ts
const isCode: (path: string) => boolean;
```

### isFix

A fix to behaviour, not to docs: `fix:`, `fix(scope):`, `fix!:`, except `fix(docs)`.

```ts
const isFix: (subject: string) => boolean;
```

### isYes

A grader answer counts as a match only when its first word is yes.

```ts
const isYes: (stdout: string) => boolean;
```

### judge

Each input's two outputs, judged: the same, a difference a person approved, or a difference.

```ts
const judge: (runs: readonly {
    readonly input: string;
    readonly base: Output;
    readonly head: Output;
}[], config: Pick<CompareConfig, "normalize" | "approved">) => CompareReport;
```

### KINDS

```ts
const KINDS: readonly ["bug", "control"];
```

### mine

Cluster findings into candidates: every pair of neighbouring content words seen in `minPrs` or
more pull requests, most pull requests first. A pair whose pull requests all sit under a pair
already drafted is the same pattern again and is dropped, so each cluster is drafted once.

```ts
const mine: (findings: readonly Finding[], options: MineOptions) => Candidate[];
```

### normalised

The output as compared: its exit code and both streams, each match of a pattern replaced by `<n>`.

```ts
const normalised: (output: Output, patterns: readonly string[]) => string;
```

### oldRanges

The old-side lines of a `git diff -U0` in code files that a fix removed or changed, skipping inert ones, as ranges.

```ts
const oldRanges: (diff: string) => OldRange[];
```

### parseCase

Read one case from its YAML; `source` names it in every error.

```ts
const parseCase: (source: string, yaml: string) => Case;
```

### parseComments

The lines `gh api --jq` printed, one JSON comment each; a blank line is skipped.

```ts
const parseComments: (lines: string) => Comment[];
```

```ts
const parseCompareConfig: (source: string, yaml: string) => CompareConfig;
```

### propose

Bug drafts for every blamed pull request found on main, newest first, alternating test and tune
so neither set is all old or all new; and per bug, the nearest-sized unblamed pull request as its
control, never one used twice.

```ts
const propose: (commits: readonly Commit[], limit: number) => Proposal;
```

### prose

What a reviewer wrote, without the machinery around it: HTML comments, folded `<details>` (a
bot's prompt for an agent), fenced code (a suggested patch), tags, badge lines and status lines.

```ts
const prose: (body: string) => string;
```

Every `*.yaml` case under `dir`, sorted by file name, each named `<id>.yaml`.

```ts
const readCases: (repo: string, dir: string) => Case[];
```

### RULE_BOTS

a repeat of theirs is a rule that works, not one that is missing.


### runCheck

The config and every case parse, each case file is named by its id, no answer is the draft's
placeholder, ids are distinct, and each set holds a bug and a control: what a run needs. A set of
one kind gives a score of one kind, recall with no false alarms or the reverse.

```ts
const runCheck: (options: CheckOptions) => Data;
```

### wordsOf

The content words of a finding, in order, lower-cased: code spans and links lose their marks but
keep their words, and paths, line numbers and hashes are dropped, because the pattern is what was
wrong, not where.

```ts
const wordsOf: (text: string) => string[];
```

## Interfaces

### Approval

One difference a person accepted: the input, the two outputs it was between, and why.

```ts
interface Approval {
    readonly input: string;
    readonly base: string;
    readonly head: string;
    readonly reason: string;
}
```

### Candidate

A pattern seen in two or more pull requests.

```ts
interface Candidate {
    /** The two content words the findings share, as a reviewer wrote them. */
    readonly phrase: string;
    readonly prs: readonly number[];
    /** One finding per pull request, newest pull request first. */
    readonly examples: readonly Finding[];
}
```

### Case

```ts
interface Case {
    readonly id: string;
    readonly kind: (typeof KINDS)[number];
    /** The pull request the commits belong to. */
    readonly pr: number;
    /** The commit the pull request was reviewed against. */
    readonly base: string;
    /** The commit the reviewer saw: the pull request applied to `base`. */
    readonly head: string;
    /** What the bug is, in one sentence. Bugs only. */
    readonly answer?: string | undefined;
    readonly set: (typeof SETS)[number];
}
```

### CaseResult

```ts
interface CaseResult {
    readonly case: Case;
    readonly findings: readonly Graded[];
    /** More findings than the cap: those past it were not graded. */
    readonly capped: boolean;
    /** Each check's id, and whether it failed on this case. */
    readonly fired: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>>;
}
```

### Comment

One review comment on a pull request, as the `gh api` queries in `GH_QUERIES` print it.

```ts
interface Comment {
    readonly pr: number;
    readonly author: string;
    readonly body: string;
    /** A reply in a review thread restates its parent, so it is not a finding of its own. */
    readonly reply: boolean;
    /** Inline: anchored to a diff line, so the whole comment is one finding. */
    readonly inline: boolean;
}
```

### Commit

One commit on main.

```ts
interface Commit {
    readonly sha: string;
    readonly parent: string;
    readonly subject: string;
    readonly body: string;
    /** Lines added and removed. */
    readonly size: number;
}
```

### CompareConfig

```ts
interface CompareConfig {
    /** Run first in each tree, which may start without node_modules or a build. */
    readonly setup?: string | undefined;
    /** Run once per input, with the input on stdin and its path in `$REPLZ_INPUT`. */
    readonly command: string;
    /** The folder of inputs, under the repository: every file in it is one input. */
    readonly inputs: string;
    /** Regular expressions whose matches are replaced in both outputs before they are compared. */
    readonly normalize: readonly string[];
    readonly approved: readonly Approval[];
}
```

### CompareReport

```ts
interface CompareReport {
    readonly inputs: number;
    readonly same: number;
    /** Differences a person approved, by input. */
    readonly approved: readonly string[];
    /** Differences nobody approved: each fails the run. */
    readonly differs: readonly Difference[];
    /** Approvals that matched no difference: the outputs moved on, so the entry can go. */
    readonly stale: readonly Approval[];
}
```

### Config

```ts
interface Config {
    /** Run first in each case's worktree, which starts without node_modules. */
    readonly setup?: string | undefined;
    readonly reviewer: string;
    /** `{model}` in it is replaced by the model a run grades with. */
    readonly grader: string;
    /** The default for `--model`. Left out, a run must name one. */
    readonly model?: string | undefined;
    readonly maxFindings: number;
    /** The reviewer's stages, in order; the last is what ships. */
    readonly stages: readonly string[];
    readonly checks: readonly Check[];
    /** The checklist whose items a finding may name, so an item that never fires is reported too. */
    readonly checklist?: string | undefined;
}
```

### Difference

```ts
interface Difference {
    readonly input: string;
    /** The digests to approve it by. */
    readonly base: string;
    readonly head: string;
    readonly at: ReturnType<typeof firstDifference>;
}
```

### Finding

One thing the reviewer said, at one stage of its pipeline.

```ts
interface Finding {
    readonly stage: string;
    readonly severity: Severity;
    readonly text: string;
    /** The checklist item that prompted it, when the reviewer says. */
    readonly item?: string | undefined;
}
```

### MinedFinding

One finding: what a reviewer said about one pull request.

```ts
interface Finding {
    readonly pr: number;
    readonly author: string;
    readonly text: string;
}
```

### Output

What one tree printed for one input.

```ts
interface Output {
    readonly code: number | null;
    readonly stdout: string;
    readonly stderr: string;
}
```

### Ratchet

The bands a scorecard is held to: the escape rate may not rise, receipts and recall may not fall.

```ts
interface Ratchet {
    readonly maxEscapeRate?: number;
    readonly minReceipts?: number;
    readonly minRecall?: number;
}
```

### Replayer

What every case of one run shares.

```ts
interface Replayer {
    readonly shell: Shell;
    readonly worktrees: Worktrees;
    readonly config: Config;
    /** Put into the grader command's `{model}`. */
    readonly model: string | undefined;
    /**
     * The repository replz was started in, as an absolute path: `REPLZ_REPO` for every command, so a
     * reviewer script kept in it is found from a case's worktree, where it may not exist yet.
     */
    readonly repo?: string | undefined;
}
```

### Report

```ts
interface Report {
    readonly bugs: number;
    readonly controls: number;
    readonly recall: readonly {
        readonly stage: string;
        readonly found: number;
    }[];
    /** Findings at the last stage, by severity. */
    readonly severity: Readonly<Record<Severity, number>>;
    /** Controls with a must-fix or should-fix finding at the last stage. */
    readonly falseAlarms: number;
    readonly firing: readonly Firing[];
    readonly neverFired: readonly string[];
    readonly capped: readonly string[];
}
```

### Scorecard

```ts
interface Scorecard {
    readonly since: string;
    readonly merged: number;
    readonly fixes: number;
    /** Fixes that added lines only, so SZZ has nothing to blame. */
    readonly untraced: number;
    readonly escapes: readonly Escape[];
    readonly escapeRate: Measure;
    readonly receipts: Measure;
    readonly recall: Measure;
    readonly falseAlarms: Measure;
    /** Escapes in the window by triage status. */
    readonly triage: {
        readonly confirmed: number;
        readonly dismissed: number;
        readonly suspect: number;
    };
    /** Escapes in the window that are neither a case nor dismissed: the triage backlog, newest first. */
    readonly uncased: readonly number[];
    /** Merged pull requests without a receipt, newest first. */
    readonly unreceipted: readonly number[];
}
```

### Worktrees

```ts
interface Worktrees {
    /** A detached worktree at `ref`, and the function that removes it. */
    readonly add: (ref: string) => Promise<{
        readonly dir: string;
        readonly remove: () => Promise<void>;
    }>;
}
```

## Types

### Severity

```ts
type Severity = (typeof SEVERITIES)[number];
```

### Shell

Runs a shell command line; a test passes its own and runs nothing.

```ts
type Shell = (command: string, options: {
    readonly cwd: string;
    readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    readonly input?: string;
}) => Promise<Ran>;
```
